newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Tractebel statutes to guarantee independence.
newsitem.headline: Tractebel statutes to guarantee independence.

text.p: Belgian utility holding company Tractebel SA said in a statement on Tuesday that its shareholders want to adapt Tractebel's statutes in order to guarantee its independence following the merger of Compagnie de Suez and Lyonnaise des Eaux.
The board also plans to propose a five for one share split.

"The board has noted with pleasure that the chairmen of Suez, Lyonnaise and Generale de Belgique (SGB) have unanimously proposed that Tractebel should continue its strategy and that the group would have the necessary management autonomy for this," the statement said.
"It is in this context that the board has taken note of the principles on the basis of which SGB proposes to change Tractebel's statutes," it added.
Suez owns 63 percent of SGB which owns 65 percent of Tractebel.
Last Friday Suez and Lyonnaise said they planned to merge.

The merger plan has led to concern in Belgium that Tractebel's domestic and foreign expansion would be blocked by Lyonnaise, a French utilities group which focuses on water. Tractebel is mainly active in the electricity sector.

In a separate statement SGB said its relations with Suez-Lyonnaise would remain unchanged. It also confirmed that it planned to propose changes to Tractebel's statutes aimed at defining its management autonomy.
Tractebel's board met to approve Tractebel's planned merger with its Powerfin unit.
The board will convene an extraordinary general meeting for May 29 to proceed with the merger, which will take the form of a takeover of Powerfin by Tractebel, the statement said.
The board also decided to propose to shareholders to split the Tractebel share at a rate of five for one to make it more accessible to investors, the statement said.
A second extraordinary general meeting is scheduled for June 20, which will vote on the proposed statutory changes.
